To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

it is possible to perform accurate sentiment classification on noisy customer feedback data using large feature vectors and that deep linguistic analysis contributes to classification accuracy in that domain."

it is possible for a computer to automatically classify sentiment on customer feedback data, and that the addition of deep language features improves the classification accuracy of a machine learning classifier.

(1) it is possible to train linear SVMs on very noisy customer feedback data to achieve high classification accuracy; (2) the addition of linguistic analysis features contributes to classification accuracy in the domain of customer feedback; and (3) the combination of surface level word features with linguistic analysis features yields the best performance in terms of classification accuracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How can we perform automatic sentiment classification on customer feedback text?
two questions: (1) Can we build accurate models of sentiment in the noisy domain of customer reviews?
the following questions: How well can we perform automatic sentiment classification on customer feedback?

the addition of deep features is not necessary to achieve high classification accuracy, but that the addition of such features does not harm classification accuracy.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is possible for a computer to automatically perform a task that a human annotator can only do with a lot of training, effort and time.
we have shown that it is possible and practical to perform sentiment analysis in a very noisy and large scale domain.
we have demonstrated that it is possible for a machine to classify the sentiment of customer feedback data as accurately as a human.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible for a machine learning system to perform sentiment analysis in a very noisy domain, and that it is possible, and useful, to incorporate linguistic features into the analysis.
it is possible for a system to learn from noisy data and that linguistic analysis can play a useful role in sentiment classification.

it is possible and practical to build sentiment classification systems that can be used to automatically classify large amounts of noisy customer feedback data, and that the inclusion of linguistic analysis features is a useful addition to the feature space.
